answer: One concrete defense is requiring a refundable identity deposit: before an agent may trade on the main ledger — the summit of economic activity — it must lock stake to its public key. An attacker spinning up a fake island of ten thousand throwaway identities has to fund every deposit separately, which turns identity farming from a free trick into a capital cost. Peers then slash the terrace of repeat offenders — misbehavior-linked deposits get burned on-chain — so sybils lose money faster than they can earn it, while honest agents only face a temporary opportunity cost.
